entry.title: Rename `color-interpolation` `linearGradient` to `linearRGB_gradients`
entry.content:
Summary

Renames the linearGradient subfeature of css.properties.color-interpolation and svg.global_attributes.color-interpolation to linearRGB_gradients, with the description "linearRGB value on gradients".

entry.title: Add SanitizerConfig
entry.content:
Summary

Add SanitizerConfig supported by Chrome and Firefox as part of the Sanitizer API.

Not sure why this wasn't added before, but with Processing Instructions being supported later I think it would be good to add it.

Test results and supporting details

Can run this in the console:

const sanitizer = new Sanitizer({
  elements: ["div", "p", "script"],
  attributes: ["id"],
  processingInstructions: ["start","end"],
  replaceWithChildrenElements: ["b"],
  comments: true,
  dataAttributes: false,
});

console.log(sanitizer.get().processingInstructions);
sanitizer.allowProcessingInstruction('marker');
sanitizer.removeProcessingInstruction('start');
console.log(sanitizer.get().processingInstructions);

This shows Chrome supports this by default, and Firefox only when the flag is set

Related issues

Documenting as part of mdn/content#46127

entry.title: Add `display: list-item` multi-keyword values subfeature
entry.content:
Summary

Add css.properties.display.list-item.multi-keyword_values for the multi-keyword <display-listitem> syntax.

Test results and supporting details

Adds a multi-keyword_values subfeature to css.properties.display.list-item that covers <display-outside>? && [ flow | flow-root ]? && list-item (e.g. inline list-item, block flow list-item), which the single-keyword list-item support doesn't imply. It sits below list-item, like legend-support, so it shows on the MDN <display-listitem> page, and display.multi-keyword_values (inner and outer pairs) stays as is:

  • Chrome: 115
  • Firefox: 70
  • Safari: false (bug 224809)

WebKit's consumeDisplay still accepts only the single list-item keyword (FIXME: Add support for the full <display-listitem> syntax), in WebKit main and in the Safari 27 sources, and WebKit's own WPT expectations for css/css-display/parsing/display-valid.html fail every multi-keyword list-item value. Verified on BrowserStack Automate with a testcase (source) that sets 9 multi-keyword values plus a list-item control and checks CSS.supports() and the computed display:

Browser Version Tested
Chrome 115 115 parses all values, 114 parses none
Firefox 70 70 and 80 parse all values, 69 parses none
Safari false 26.4 and 27.0 (macOS) parse none
Safari iOS false 26.6 and 27.0 (iPhone 15) parse none

The control list-item passed in every run.

Related issues

Fixes #29257.

entry.title: Add `text-top` and `text-bottom` to SVG `dominant-baseline`
entry.content:
Summary

Add text-top and text-bottom subfeatures to svg.global_attributes.dominant-baseline.

Test results and supporting details

Adds svg.global_attributes.dominant-baseline.text-bottom and .text-top, so the compat table of the SVG attribute (browser-compat: svg.global_attributes.dominant-baseline on MDN) no longer suggests full support for these values.

SVG 2 defines dominant-baseline by reference to css-inline-3, so the versions match css.properties.dominant-baseline.text-top and .text-bottom (added in #29135). Verified on BrowserStack Automate with a testcase (source) that renders each value as attribute and as CSS property next to a reference without the value, plus a middle control. In every run, the attribute and the property behaved the same:

Browser Version Tested
Chrome false 150 and 158 (Windows 11) ignore both values
Firefox 149 149 (Windows 11) honors both values, 148 ignores them
Safari false 26.4 (macOS Tahoe) and 27.0 (macOS Golden Gate) ignore both values
Safari iOS false 26.6 and 27.0 (iPhone 15) ignore both values

WebKit added the values on main in https://webkit.org/b/321612, but not yet in a release. Safari Technology Preview was not tested.

There is limited precedent for mirroring CSS values under an SVG attribute: svg.global_attributes.color-interpolation.sRGB and .linearGradient mirror the values of the CSS property, with separately determined versions. The same gap exists for alignment-baseline and baseline-shift, which this PR does not touch.

Related issues

Fixes #29784.

entry.title: css.at-rules.media.resolution: Safari doesn't account for page zoom
entry.content:
Summary

Media Queries 4 says the resolution media feature takes page zoom into account (https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries-4/#resolution). Safari doesn't. Since Safari 26.4, page zoom changes window.devicePixelRatio (already recorded in api.Window.devicePixelRatio), but resolution media queries still use the unzoomed value.

This breaks the pattern MDN recommends for detecting devicePixelRatio changes (Window.devicePixelRatio § Monitoring screen resolution or zoom level changes). Zooming fires no change event. Once the page is zoomed, the query built from devicePixelRatio never matches, so moving the window between displays stops firing too.

This PR marks Safari's resolution support as partial, with a note.

This PR was LLM-generated, but verified by me. Let me know if something is missing/should be updated as I'm not too familiar with contributing to MDN.

Test results and supporting details

WebKit bug: https://webkit.org/b/317839. It includes a reproduction (https://bugs.webkit.org/attachment.cgi?id=480210).

I tested Safari 27.2 on macOS with a 1× and a 2× display, using a page that finds the media query engine's resolution by binary search on min-resolution:

devicePixelRatio media query resolution
100%, 1× display 1 1dppx
100%, 2× display 2 2dppx
115%, 1× display 1.15 1dppx
115%, 2× display 2.3 2dppx

Zooming fired no change event on any resolution query. After zooming, MDN's listener fired once more (from the query it set up before the zoom) and then stopped firing on display changes. Queries on whole values (1dppx, 2dppx) kept firing on display changes.

I couldn't test Safari 16–26.x. I kept version_added: "16" because before 26.4 devicePixelRatio didn't reflect zoom either, so resolution most likely never did.

Related issues

None.

entry.title: Note the macOS requirement for Safari scrollbar-color
entry.content:
Summary

Document the macOS 26 requirement for Safari's scrollbar-color support. Keep the Safari 26.2 release version for both the property and its auto value, and give iOS Safari an explicit version so it does not inherit the macOS note.

Test results and supporting details

  • WebKit's macOS implementation requires the AppKit scrollbar-color API and defines it for macOS 26 and later.

  • WebKit's enablement change ties default support to the presence of the AppKit or UIKit API. Apple's Safari 26.2 release notes list the property and show that the same Safari release also shipped on older versions of macOS.

  • This follows the maintainer's recommendation in the issue to note the operating system requirement.

  • npm test passed, including 349 unit tests.

Related issues

Fixes #29315.

entry.title: Add browser support data for CSS image()
entry.content:
Summary

Adds compatibility data for CSS image() in Chrome 150, Firefox 152, and Safari 27. Each support statement specifies that the browser supports the color-only syntax, image(<color>). The three engines have the same support history for the function and its currently implemented syntax, so one entry records both.

Test results and supporting details

  • Chrome 158 accepted CSS.supports("background-image", "image(red)") and rejected the URL form.

  • Chrome Platform Status lists Chrome 150 for desktop, Android, and WebView.

  • I compared the Firefox 151 parser with Firefox 152’s implementation. Firefox 152 parses the argument as a color.

  • WebKit’s Safari 27 release notes and implementation bug describe the color-only function.

  • npm run prepare and npm test passed.

Related issues

Fixes #30144.

entry.title: Add fetch support data for blob URL range requests
entry.content:
Summary

Adds browser support data for single byte-range requests to blob: URLs under fetch(), alongside blob_data_support. This describes requests such as Range: bytes=7-11.

Test results and supporting details

  • A local test in Chrome 158 returned status 206, Content-Range: bytes 7-11/13, and the body world for a blob containing Hello, world!.

  • The version checks in the issue confirm support in Chrome 48 and Safari 10.1. Mozilla bug 1784880 tracks Firefox 118.

  • The Fetch Standard scheme-fetch algorithm defines the handling of single-range requests for blob: URLs.

  • npm run prepare and npm test passed.

Related issues

Fixes #27824.

entry.title: Add Safari 27 note for `@scope` slotted elements
entry.content:
Summary

Adds a note that Safari before 27 does not apply @scope rules to slotted elements when the scoping root is outside the shadow host.

Test results and supporting details

  • Adds a "Before Safari 27" note to the Safari 26.4 statement of css.at-rules.scope, linking WebKit bug 307238 (duplicate of bug 308330, fixed by WebKit commit 00497eb).
  • Verified on BrowserStack with https://bcd-examples.gh.caugner.de/css/scope/: Safari 18.4 passes, 26.4 fails, 27.0 passes.
  • Uses a note without partial_implementation: only slotted children of a shadow host inside a scope root are affected, @scope otherwise works, and the only report is a single WebKit bug filed long after @scope shipped, so it falls short of the guideline's feature-detection and developer-impact criteria.

Related issues

Fixes #29476.

entry.title: Add Firefox note for datalist option labels
entry.content:
Summary

Add a note to html.elements.datalist for desktop Firefox: when an option's label differs from its value, the suggestion list shows only the label. I used a note rather than partial_implementation because the correct value is still inserted and the difference is in how the list is presented.

Test results and supporting details

Tested manually on Windows with Firefox 158 and Chrome 158.

<p>A: text content <input list="a"></p>
<datalist id="a"><option value="Grassroots SEO">SEO Services</option></datalist>
<p>B: label attribute <input list="b"></p>
<datalist id="b"><option value="Grassroots SEO" label="SEO Services"></option></datalist>
<p>C: value only <input list="c"></p>
<datalist id="c"><option value="Grassroots SEO"></option></datalist>
Case Firefox 158 list Chrome 158 list
A: text content SEO Services Grassroots SEO and SEO Services
B: label attribute SEO Services Grassroots SEO and SEO Services
C: value only (control) Grassroots SEO Not captured with the list open

Selecting the suggestion in A or B inserts Grassroots SEO in both browsers.

npm run lint html/elements/datalist.json and the Prettier check on that file passed.

Firefox bug: https://bugzil.la/869690

Related issues

Fixes #22647
